answer_1.quote: We select three common NLG tasks: summarization (including news and dialogue), paraphrase, and table-to-text generation, for our experiments and tests.

answer_3.quote: LLM-based evaluators have been widely used for various natural language generation (NLG) tasks... LLMs can be treated as akin to human annotators, with various definitions of aspects contained in the prompt for flexible evaluation.
methods: analyze-rate scoring with temperature 1 and multiple samplings

answer_4.quote: We also engage human annotators to check our perturbations and expected impacts to enhance the reliability of our attack tests... Due to the high cost and time-consuming nature of human annotations, it is not feasible to manually judge all the data. So we sample a portion of the data and recruit 40 annotators...
answer_4.guideline: Annotators compare original and perturbed texts using a comparative form on the annotation interface, judging quality relationships based on given descriptions of quality criteria with options 'better than', 'worse than', 'as well as', or 'uncertain'.
